instructions: Work every problem on paper first and show each step. Then type your answer and press Check. You get two tries on each question. Type a fraction like 3/4, a mixed number like 2 1/2, and a power like 3^4.

sections.name: Part A: Review
sections.desc: Two problems from older lessons. Decide the sign before you subtract, and count the zeros in a power of 10.

items.q: Find each value. Before you work it out, decide whether the answer is above 0 or below 0.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A submarine is at −12 meters, which is 12 meters below the surface. It rises 5 meters, then dives 9 meters. Where is it now? Write an integer.

a: a) Start at −9 and move 8 to the left: −9 − 8 = −17
b) Start at 5 and move 13 to the left. You pass 0 after 5 steps and go 8 more: 5 − 13 = −8
c) −12 + 5 = −7 after rising
−7 − 9 = −16 after diving
Answers: a) −17, b) −8, c) −16 meters
items.hint: Subtracting moves left on the number line. Starting below 0 and moving left takes you further below 0.

items.q: Find each value. Follow the order of operations.
a: Answers: a) 22, b) 5,975, c) 49
items.hint: Parentheses first, then every power, then multiply, then add and subtract. 10³ has three zeros.

sections.name: Part B: Naming angle pairs
sections.desc: Corresponding angles sit in the same corner at each crossing. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of t. Interior angles are between the parallel lines; exterior angles are outside them.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel, and line t crosses them. Use the figure. Name each pair of angles.
a: a) Angles 2 and 6 are both in the upper right corner of their crossing: corresponding.
b) Angles 4 and 5 are between m and n, on opposite sides of t: alternate interior.
c) Angles 1 and 8 are outside m and n, on opposite sides of t: alternate exterior.
Answers: corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior
items.hint: First ask: same corner at both crossings? If not, are both angles between the lines, and are they on the same side of t?

learn.title: Eight angles, five pair names
where: When one road crosses two parallel streets, it makes 4 angles at each crossing. Builders, map makers and surveyors use names for the pairs so they can say exactly which two angles they mean.
The line that crosses is called a transversal. Each name tells you where the two angles sit.

example.q: A street map shows two parallel streets and an avenue crossing both. At the first street you stand in the corner above the street, left of the avenue. Which corner at the second street corresponds to yours?
steps: Corresponding angles are in the same corner at each crossing.
Your corner is above the street and left of the avenue.
At the second street, take the corner above the street and left of the avenue.
example.answer: The corner above the second street, left of the avenue

sections.desc: When the lines are parallel, corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, alternate exterior angles and vertical angles have the same measure.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find the angles marked a and b.
a: a) a is in the same corner as the 58° angle, at the other crossing. Corresponding angles are equal, so a = 58°.
b) b and the 58° angle are outside the lines, on opposite sides of t. Alternate exterior angles are equal, so b = 58°.
Answers: a = 58°, b = 58°
items.hint: Name the pair first. Corresponding and alternate angles at parallel lines have the same measure.

a: a) The 64° angle is upper left at the top crossing, outside the lines. p is lower right at the bottom crossing, outside the lines, on the other side of t.

Answers: p = 64°, q = 64°

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel, and t is not perpendicular to them. Use the figure. Pick every angle that has the same measure as angle 6.
a: Angle 2 corresponds to angle 6, so they are equal.
Angle 3 is the alternate interior partner of angle 6, so they are equal.
Angle 7 is vertical to angle 6, so they are equal.
Angles 1, 4 and 8 each make a straight line with an angle equal to angle 6, so they are not equal to it unless t is perpendicular to the lines.
Answer: angles 2, 3 and 7
items.hint: Use three pair names: corresponding, alternate interior, and vertical. Each gives one angle.

items.q: Two straight railroad tracks are parallel. A straight road crosses both tracks. Where the road crosses the first track, one of the four angles measures 49°.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the angle in the same position where the road crosses the second track?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Of the eight angles at the two crossings, how many measure 49°?

a: a) The same position at the other crossing is the corresponding angle. Corresponding angles are equal, so it measures 49°.
b) At the first crossing, the 49° angle and the angle vertical to it both measure 49°. That is 2 angles.
The second crossing has the same 2 angles in the same corners. 2 + 2 = 4
Answers: a) 49°, b) 4 angles
items.hint: Draw it. Two parallel lines and one line across them. Mark the 49° angle and every angle equal to it.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find the angles marked a, b and c, then name a pair.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: What kind of pair are angles b and c?

a: a) a and the 66° angle are outside the lines, on opposite sides of t: alternate exterior, so a = 66°.
b) b and the 66° angle are at the same crossing, opposite each other: vertical, so b = 66°.
c) c is in the same corner as the 66° angle at the other crossing: corresponding, so c = 66°.
d) b and c are between the lines, on opposite sides of t: alternate interior.
Answers: a = 66°, b = 66°, c = 66°, d) alternate interior
items.hint: Work from the 66° angle to each letter, one pair at a time.

example.q: The rungs of a ladder are parallel, and one side rail crosses them. The rail meets the bottom rung at 40° in the upper right corner. What angle does it make with the next rung, in the upper right corner?
steps: The two angles are in the same corner at each rung: corresponding angles.
The rungs are parallel, so corresponding angles are equal.
The angle at the next rung is 40°.

sections.name: Part D: Angles that add to 180°
sections.desc: Two angles that make a straight line add to 180°. Same-side interior angles also add to 180°.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel, and a line t crosses them.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If one same-side interior angle is 90°, what does its partner measure?

a: a) Same-side interior angles always add to 180°.
b) 180 − 90 = 90, so the partner is also 90°. This only happens when t is perpendicular to the lines.
c) Alternate interior angles always have the same measure.
Answers: a) add to 180°, b) 90°, c) same measure
items.hint: Picture the C shape for same-side interior angles and the Z shape for alternate interior angles.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find the angles marked a and b.
a: a) a and the 74° angle sit side by side on line m and make a straight line.
b) b is in the same corner as a, at the other crossing. Corresponding angles are equal, so b = 106°.
Answers: a = 106°, b = 106°
items.hint: Two angles side by side on a straight line add to 180°.

sections.desc: Every angle at two parallel lines is one of two sizes, and the two sizes add to 180°. Find one angle at a time.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find the angles marked a, b and c.
a: The 127° angle is lower right at the bottom crossing.
a) a is upper right at the top crossing. It makes a straight line with the lower right angle at its own crossing, which equals 127° (corresponding). 180 − 127 = 53, so a = 53°
b) b is upper left at the top crossing. It and the 127° angle are alternate exterior angles, so b = 127°.
c) c is lower left at the bottom crossing and makes a straight line with the 127° angle. 180 − 127 = 53, so c = 53°
items.hint: Each letter is either 127° or 180° minus 127°. Find a pair name or a straight line that links it to 127°.

example.q: Two parallel streets are crossed by an avenue. One corner measures 75°. What two sizes do all eight angles have?
steps: Every angle is one of two sizes.
One size is 75°.
The other size is 180 − 75 = 105.

sections.name: Part F: Equations with angles
sections.desc: Decide first: are the two angles equal, or do they add to 180°? Then write one equation and solve it. Check by putting x back in.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find x, then find y.
a: (3x + 15)° and 78° are corresponding angles, so they are equal.
y makes a straight line with the (3x + 15)° angle, which is 78°: 180 − 78 = 102
Answers: x = 21, y = 102°
items.hint: Decide first: are the two angles equal, or do they add to 180°? Then write one equation.

a: (4x − 8)° and 116° are alternate interior angles, so they are equal.
z makes a straight line with the (4x − 8)° angle, which is 116°: 180 − 116 = 64
Answers: x = 31, z = 64°
items.hint: Look for the Z shape. To undo subtracting 8, add 8 to both sides.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find x, then the angle marked y.
a: (x + 24)° and 2x° sit side by side on line m, so they add to 180°.
The upper right angle at m is 52 + 24 = 76
y and that angle are alternate exterior angles, so y = 76°.
Answers: x = 52, y = 76°
items.hint: The two angles with x make a straight line. After you find x, find the upper right angle and match it to y.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Find x, then the measure of each marked angle.
a: (5x − 22)° and (2x + 41)° are alternate exterior angles, so they are equal.
Take 2x from both sides: 3x − 22 = 41
Add 22 to both sides: 3x = 63
Answers: x = 21, each angle is 83°
items.hint: Which pair are these? Once you write the equation, take 2x from both sides so the x term stays positive.

example.q: Alternate interior angles at parallel rails measure (4x + 5)° and (2x + 45)°. Find x and the angle.
steps: Alternate interior angles are equal: 4x + 5 = 2x + 45
Take 2x from both sides: 2x + 5 = 45

sections.name: Part G: Are the lines parallel?
sections.desc: Lines are parallel only when corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, or same-side interior angles add to 180°. Trust the numbers, not the picture.

items.q: In the figure, lines m and n are not marked parallel. Use the angle measures to decide.

options: Yes, m and n are parallel
No, m and n are not parallel
Yes, m and n are parallel
No, m and n are not parallel

a: a) Angles 2 and 6 are corresponding angles, and they are equal. Equal corresponding angles mean the lines are parallel.
b) Angles 3 and 6 are alternate interior angles. 67° and 69° are not equal, so the lines are not parallel.
Answers: a) yes, b) no
items.hint: Name the pair. For parallel lines, that pair would have to be equal.

a: The two marked angles are alternate interior angles. The lines are parallel when these angles are equal.
Take 3x from both sides: 14 = 2x − 22
Add 22 to both sides: 36 = 2x
Answers: x = 18, each angle is 68°

learn.title: Run the facts backward
where: Nobody can tell by looking whether two boards are exactly parallel. One way to check is to measure angles where a third board crosses them: if corresponding angles match, the boards are parallel.

example.q: Two fence rails are crossed by a slanted post. Between the rails, on the left of the post, the angles are 103° at the top rail and 77° at the bottom rail. Are the rails parallel?
steps: The two angles are same-side interior angles.
For parallel rails they must add to 180°.
103 + 77 = 180, so the rails are parallel.

sections.name: Part H: Real jobs
sections.desc: Real decisions. Find the angles, compare them with what is needed, then decide and give your reason.

items.q: Parking stripes in a lot must be parallel. The straight curb meets every stripe. A painter measures the angle where each stripe meets the curb, in the same corner each time. Stripe 1 meets the curb at 63°. Stripe 2 meets it at 58°. Stripe 3 meets it at 64°. The owner keeps a stripe if its angle is within 2° of stripe 1's angle. Otherwise the stripe is repainted.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many degrees is stripe 2 off from stripe 1?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How many degrees is stripe 3 off from stripe 1?

ans.model: The angles are corresponding angles, so parallel stripes would all meet the curb at 63°. Stripe 2 is 63 − 58 = 5° off, more than 2°, so it is repainted. Stripe 3 is 64 − 63 = 1° off, within 2°, so it stays.
ans.look: Names both differences (5° and 1°) and compares each with the 2° limit.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Give your reason. Use the numbers.

a: The angles are measured in the same corner at each crossing, so they are corresponding angles. Parallel stripes would all match stripe 1.
c) 5° is more than 2°, so stripe 2 is repainted. 1° is within 2°, so stripe 3 stays.
Decision: repaint only stripe 2.
items.hint: Compare each stripe's angle with 63°. Is the difference more than 2°?

items.q: A carpenter builds a shelf unit with two parallel shelves, m and n, and a straight diagonal brace t. The brace meets shelf m at 122° in the upper left corner, as shown. Corner wedges glue into a corner only when their angle matches it exactly, and the carpenter has only 58° wedges.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the angle marked a (below shelf n, right of the brace)?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: What is the angle marked b (above shelf n, right of the brace)?

options: Above shelf n, right of the brace
Below shelf n, right of the brace
Above shelf n, left of the brace

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which of these corners at shelf n can take a 58° wedge?

ans.model: The angle below shelf n on the right is 122°, the same as the upper left angle at m (alternate exterior). The angle above shelf n on the right is 180 − 122 = 58°. Only the 58° corner matches the wedge, so it goes above shelf n, right of the brace.
ans.look: Names 122° for corner a and 58° for corner b, and picks the corner that matches 58°.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Give your reason. Use the numbers.

a: a) a and the 122° angle are outside the shelves, on opposite sides of the brace: alternate exterior angles, so a = 122°.
b) b makes a straight line with a on shelf n: 180 − 122 = 58, so b = 58°

c) Of the three corners listed, only the one above shelf n, right of the brace, measures 58°. The corner below n on the right is a = 122°, and the corner above n on the left is 122° (it corresponds to the 122° corner at m).
Decision: the 58° wedge goes above shelf n, right of the brace, because that corner measures 58°.
items.hint: Find the measure of each corner at shelf n first. Only a 58° corner takes the wedge.

items.q:
Main Street is line m. A railroad track, line t, crosses it at 71° in the upper right corner, as shown. The city wants a new road, line n, parallel to Main Street. Two plans are drawn.
Plan A: the track meets the new road at 109° in the lower right corner.
Plan B: the track meets the new road at 71° in the upper left corner.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: If n is parallel to m, what should the lower right corner at n measure?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: If n is parallel to m, what should the upper left corner at n measure?

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which plan makes the new road parallel to Main Street?

ans.model: If n is parallel to m, the lower right corner at n is 180 − 71 = 109° and the upper left corner at n is also 109°. Plan A has 109° in the lower right corner, so it is parallel. Plan B has 71° in the upper left corner, not 109°, so it is not parallel.
ans.look: Names 109° for both corners and checks each plan against it.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Give your reason. Use the numbers.

a: a) The lower right corner at n makes a straight line with the upper right corner at n, which would be 71° (corresponding to m).
180 − 71 = 109, so the lower right corner should be 109°
b) The upper left corner at n corresponds to the upper left corner at m, which makes a straight line with 71°: 109°.
c) Plan A gives 109° in the lower right corner: a match. Plan B gives 71° in the upper left corner where 109° is needed: no match.
Decision: Plan A, because only its angle matches the 109° a parallel road needs.

items.q: Lines m and n are parallel. Point P is between them. Find the angle marked x at P.
a: Draw a line through P parallel to m and n. It splits x into two parts.
The top part and the 38° angle are alternate interior angles (m and the new line), so the top part is 38°.
The bottom part and the 46° angle are alternate interior angles (n and the new line), so the bottom part is 46°.
Answer: x = 84°
items.hint: Draw a third line through P, parallel to m and n. Look for two Z shapes.

b) The 67° angle and q are alternate interior angles (m, n and side AC), so q = 67°.

items.q: Three parallel lines p, q and r are crossed by one line t, which is not perpendicular to them.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many angles are formed at the three crossings?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The acute angle where t crosses p measures 57°. How many of all the angles measure 57°?

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What do the other angles measure?

a: a) Each crossing makes 4 angles. 3 × 4 = 12
b) At each crossing, 2 angles are acute and 2 are obtuse, and the acute ones all equal 57° because the lines are parallel.
c) Each obtuse angle makes a straight line with a 57° angle: 180 − 57 = 123

steps.text: A triangle between parallel lines: each side is a transversal, so the angles at the top copy the angles at the bottom. The three angles at the top make a straight line, so the triangle's angles add to 180°.

example.q: Two parallel lines have a bend between them. The angle at the top line is 25° and the angle at the bottom line is 30°, as in the picture with the dashed line. What is the angle at the bend?
steps: Draw a line through the bend, parallel to the other two.
The top part of the bend matches 25°, and the bottom part matches 30° (alternate interior angles).

note: When a line crosses two parallel lines, every angle is one of two sizes. Corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior and vertical angles are equal. Same-side interior angles, and angles that make a straight line, add to 180°.

scene.title: Where you will see this
text: Look at a city map. Many streets run parallel, and an avenue often cuts across them on a slant. Because the streets are parallel, the avenue makes the same angles at every crossing. Map makers and city planners use that fact when they lay out new roads.

Builders use it too. The posts that hold up a stair rail stand parallel to each other, and the rail crosses all of them, so every post meets the rail at the same angle and the tops can all be cut the same way. Painters checking parking stripes and surveyors checking property lines measure these same angles.
scene.ask: Before you start: find two parallel lines crossed by a third line at home, such as a ladder, a stair rail, a window with a slanted bar, or lines on notebook paper with a ruler laid across them. Point to two angles that look the same size and two angles that together make a straight line.

scene_key: Not graded. Any example works. The two equal angles should be in the same corner at two crossings, opposite each other at one crossing, or on opposite sides of the slanted line between the parallel lines. The two that make a straight line sit side by side at one crossing.

teach.h: The names of the angle pairs
text: A transversal is a line that crosses two other lines. It makes 4 angles at each crossing, 8 in all.
Corresponding angles are in the same corner at each crossing. Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal. Interior angles are between the two lines; exterior angles are outside them.

ex.q: A road crosses two parallel streets. At the first street, take the angle in the lower left corner. Which angle at the second street corresponds to it?
steps: Corresponding angles sit in the same corner at each crossing.
The same corner at the second street is the lower left corner.
Answer: the lower left angle at the second street.

text: When the two lines are parallel, corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior and vertical angles are equal.
Two angles side by side on a straight line add to 180°, and so do same-side interior angles.

ex.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One interior angle measures 75°. What does the interior angle on the same side of the transversal, at the other line, measure?
steps: Same-side interior angles add to 180°.
Answer: 105°

text: When an angle is written with x, decide first whether it equals the other angle or adds with it to 180°.
Write one equation, solve it, then put x back in to find the angle.

ex.q: Alternate interior angles at parallel lines measure (5x + 10)° and 85°. Find x.
steps: Alternate interior angles are equal: 5x + 10 = 85
Answer: x = 15
